A.metadata_summary: Early-30s woman; clear neutral American; steady conversational pace; authority plus approachability.
A.why_test: Best neutral baseline for Naomi's professional authority without overt action-hero coding.
A.known_risk: Could read too polished/corporate; must prove dry humor and private cost.

B.metadata_summary: Late-20s/early-30s woman; refined American; rich, confident, warm, intelligent.
B.why_test: Tests whether Naomi can carry female-gaze warmth while keeping command authority.
B.known_risk: May be too inviting/velvety or subtly romantic.

C.metadata_summary: Early-30s woman; crisp, efficient, alert, analytical; slight British accent.
C.why_test: Useful competence-control candidate: can test clarity and tactical precision.
C.known_risk: Accent mismatch and possible over-coolness; likely rejection if accent cannot neutralize.

design_challenger.voice_description: American woman in her early 30s, grounded low-mezzo to alto speaking voice, precise and economical. Professional close-protection authority without military cosplay, hardness, seduction, or maternal warmth. Neutral contemporary American English, crisp consonants, controlled medium-low energy, understated dry humor. Under danger she becomes clearer rather than louder. When emotionally exposed she gets slightly quieter, never breathy. Human warmth must be audible only in tiny register changes. No ethnic accent imitation.
design_challenger.preview_text: If I say “cross,” you cross to the side I name. No debate until we're clear. During danger I need compliance. Outside it, I need your agreement. I'm not selling you calm. I'm selling you choices you can still make when calm is gone.

A.metadata_summary: Early-30s man; natural American; warm, conversational, medium pitch, trustworthy.
A.why_test: Strong private-register baseline; likely to avoid announcer/alpha performance.
A.known_risk: May lack enough public-star charisma or musical edge.

B.metadata_summary: Early-30s man; warm charismatic baritone; slight California accent; confident, engaging.
B.why_test: Tests public charisma and attraction without using a celebrity imitation.
B.known_risk: Smile may remain baked into private/vulnerable register.

C.metadata_summary: Early-30s man; adaptable medium pitch; subtle international accent; friendly confidence; flexible rhythm.
C.why_test: Potentially useful for a globally famous performer who must sound natural in private and polished in public.
C.known_risk: International accent may be too noticeable or generic; must prove musician specificity.

design_challenger.voice_description: Man in his early 30s with a contemporary neutral American or very light globally cosmopolitan English accent. Attractive but natural medium-low speaking voice, stage-trained breath, musician's sense of rhythm, no announcer voice. Public speech can become polished and charismatic; private speech becomes economical, lower, and less performed. He must reveal strain through one broken rhythm or breath without sounding helpless, possessive, dominant, or melodramatic.
design_challenger.preview_text: First live show in a year, twelve thousand people outside, and half the internet waiting to decide whether I can still stand under lights. No pressure. I spent a year being told other people's decisions were my preferences. I want to hear it before someone tells me what I heard.

A.metadata_summary: Late-30s man; deep, neutral American; measured; natural authority; slight gravel.
A.why_test: Closest public-library metadata to experienced field security.
A.known_risk: Could sound too heroic/protective and telegraph a stock bodyguard.

B.metadata_summary: Late-30s/early-40s man; warm deep timbre; calm measured neutral American; slight gravel.
B.why_test: Tests non-villain plausibility and credible incumbent authority.
B.known_risk: May be too reassuring and insufficiently clipped.

C.metadata_summary: Man in his 40s; precise articulation, neutral accent, direct, competent, smooth medium pitch.
C.why_test: Cleanest test of protocol/directness without villain or thug coding.
C.known_risk: May sound like technical presenter rather than security professional.

design_challenger.voice_description: American man in his early 40s, practical field-security professional. Medium-low voice, clipped radio habits, good breath support, natural human texture, no action-movie growl. He can sound irritated and territorial about procedure without sounding guilty, sinister, bullying, or stupid. Neutral American accent, concise phrasing, credible command-room experience.
design_challenger.preview_text: We are already four behind. Threat detail comes to security first. We can reconstruct cue order later. You don't get to decide that alone.

A.metadata_summary: Late-20s woman; crisp professional American; slightly fast; clear, articulate, energetic.
A.why_test: Strong baseline for habitual cue-language speed and clarity.
A.known_risk: Could sound corporate/presentation-like rather than backstage.

B.metadata_summary: Early-30s woman; crisp, articulate, brisk; excellent breath control; professional urgency.
B.why_test: Tests pressure clarity and recoverable urgency.
B.known_risk: May sound like reporting rather than stage-control; slight mid-Atlantic accent.

C.metadata_summary: Mid-20s woman; bright, quick, clear; slight West Coast American; energetic and engaging.
C.why_test: Useful contrast for speed, spontaneous correction, and live-show energy.
C.known_risk: Age/brightness may read too young or cheerful.

design_challenger.voice_description: American woman in her early to mid 30s who has spent years calling live stage cues. Medium voice, quick but unhurried professional rhythm, crisp numbers and technical terms, headset-room authority, no presenter polish. Routine lines should feel automatic. Under real failure she permits one short panic spike, then immediately returns to exact witness precision. No pre-guilty anxiety, no melodrama.
design_challenger.preview_text: Lift B at show height. Stage-left lane clear. Stand by descent. Rehearsal bridge coming up. Dae's old export still has the four-count, so don't jump early. No. I was still on standby. I never got an acknowledgement.

A.metadata_summary: Middle-aged woman; measured, restrained; slightly lower pitch; calm and conversational.
A.why_test: Tests whether ordinary restrained humanity makes access itself frightening.
A.known_risk: Dry wit/warmth may humanize too much or imply a specific personality.

B.metadata_summary: Woman in her 30s; clear, precise, adaptable, neutral accent; subtle warmth.
B.why_test: Strong intelligibility and ordinary-human precision without inherent menace.
B.known_risk: Interest/warmth may be too perceptible for anonymous threat certainty.

C.metadata_summary: Middle-aged man; flat neutral American; expressionless, almost robotic while still human.
C.why_test: Deliberate control candidate for maximum emotional neutrality.
C.known_risk: Likely hard fail: robotic/monotone can turn mystery into gimmick or horror coding.

design_challenger.voice_description: Ordinary adult human voice that is difficult to place socially, around 30 to 45. Neutral contemporary American or nearly accentless international English. Medium pitch, extremely clear, calm declarative delivery, low emotional coloration but still unmistakably human. No whisper, no growl, no synthetic robot effect, no horror cadence, no taunting, no sarcasm. The frightening element is unauthorized access and certainty, not the sound of the speaker.
design_challenger.preview_text: At eleven forty-three, the stage will fall. Your new bodyguard arranged it. At eleven forty-three, the stage will fall. Your new bodyguard arranged it.
